notes: UNCHANGED at 90.0 on purpose (2026-10-25). The coverage MEASURE changed to product code only: [tool.coverage.run] source in pyproject.toml now limits it to src/, streamlit_app/, design-system/ and analysis/, and tests, scripts/, tools/ and .github/ no longer count (the target is product code at or above 90%). On the old basis (every imported file, the tests' own 98% among them) main read 91.12%; on this basis the same code reads roughly 84-85% (84.85% from the old payload's product files, 84.19% once never-imported files join), so the guard is expected to report a breach until the product code is tested up to the target. That breach is true, not a regression: nothing was lost, the measure got stricter. It is left visible as the standing signal rather than reset to the lower reading; the climb to 90% is tracked in the pull request that made the change. Readings from before 2026-10-25 are on the old basis and are not comparable. EARLIER NOTE, on the old basis: RAISED 85 -> 90 on 2026-08-26. Measured 90.79%, so the previous value carried 5.8 points of slack -- the contamination fix in #6006 moved this from a reported 83.33% to a real 90.79% by excluding 95 tmp-workspace rows, so the 85 predates the number being correct. A baseline far below reality cannot fail and therefore reports nothing. Set at floored measured current, leaving the jitter tolerance in warn_drop rather than in the floor. A ratchet: raise it as coverage rises, never lower it to make a run pass. Keyed `line`, which takes precedence over `coverage` in both coverage_trend.py and coverage_guard.py.
